content.title: The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist (2026) ⭐ 7.2 | Documentary
content.text: Cast & crewUser reviews2026PG-131h 43mA father-to-be tries to figure out what is happening with all this AI insanity.A father-to-be tries to figure out what is happening with all this AI insanity.A father-to-be tries to figure out what is happening with all this AI insanity.10User reviews17Critic reviews60MetascoreVideos3Featured reviewsA successful documentary: perhaps one of the last onesThis movie, or documentary, whatever you prefer to call it, is a clear illustration of how AI is changing so quickly. It doesn't dive too deep into the technical details, but that makes it accessible to a wider audience. Overall, it's a well-made documentary that explores all aspects of our shared future in the AI era. This was even rewritten using AI.Impressive BreadthThe most impressive aspects of this documentary are the sheer variety of experts who were interviewed, and the sheer importance of some of them (e.g. Sam Altman).Additionally, I applaud Roher's attempt to make sense of the issue, his willingness to change his mind, and his interest in explaining the subject's fundamentals (e.g. A. I. As pattern-recognition) before moving into discussions of policy.My primary criticism is the lack of engagement between different experts and their arguments, especially about existential/catastrophic risk. Roher, by his own admission, seems to have settled into his final position based on what feels good, not based on the quality of the doomers' and optimists' arguments.This is especially disappointing because many of the experts' other claims about A. I. are both less interesting and more spurious. For example, Karen Hao's alarm about A. I.'s water usage has been decisively debunked by Andy Masley.My other criticism of the film is the editing and visual effects, which are distracting and pointlessly frenetic, especially during the first half-hour or so.Despite the documentary's shortcomings, I think that it serves as a good introduction to and overview of A. I. issues. It explains the fundamentals well, and it covers an enormous variety of viewpoints. Consequently, it's educational who those know that don't understand the subject, and it's thought-provoking for anyone who's inclined to see A. I. regulation as a simple, partisan issue.The AI Conversation: An IntroThat's the title that I think fits best, and it did a fantastic job at that. If you want a detailed documentary on AI, this one hopefully gets the conversation going enough that such a documentary will come out very soon! For now, I can say, as someone deeply embedded in "the AI conversation" myself, that most people have absolutely no sense of the actual perils, and, without causing any heart attacks, this film addresses some of those. It's balanced, helpful, and well-paced so that people living under a rock and people who have heard tons about AI but haven't really thought deeply and seriously about it yet can get kickstarted into the conversation. It is the conversation we all need to be having now, I do believe that. If you're not well versed on AI, well you should be now lol, and this film is absolutely for you.TimelyPerfectly captures the anxiety of a parent in the face of the extremely uncertain future of AI. Not a technical view, but an emotional one. He did the CEOs of the AI companies a bit dirty with the edits but oh well. Beautiful and artistic discussion of the topic. If you don't understand what's coming please watch this, now.A view from an AI researcherI sat down for what I expected to be a lazy Tuesday movie night, but this film delivered more intellectual stimulation than many high-profile AI podcasts featuring research pioneers. Daniel's contribution stood out in particular instead of delivering another dry technical summary, he articulated a deeply subjective and human-centered worldview with genuine clarity and conviction.I believe both endings presented in the film are ultimately correct, each capturing a different facet of our relationship with AI. Humans are emotional creatures by nature. Traits like sympathy, anxiety, jealousy, and the full spectrum of complex feelings cannot be authentically replicated by today's AI systems. Even advanced techniques like chain-of-thought prompting remain sophisticated mimicry - useful for solving 1+1=2, but no substitute for genuine understanding or lived experience.The younger generation (Gen Beta especially) will undoubtedly benefit enormously from AI tools, yet they risk a quiet erosion of critical thinking. When reality and synthetic content become increasingly difficult to distinguish, children may grow up struggling to separate what is real from what is generated, a challenge that only becomes clear once they reach full maturity.On the other hand, Caroline's perspective that we must actively upgrade ourselves is equally compelling and, in my view, essential. To thrive in this third AI revolution, one must first understand what AI is, how to use it effectively, and why it produces the outputs it does based on our prompts. True participation demands going further: becoming an AI researcher or at least developing a researcher's mindset.That said, the voices featured in the film naturally represent a somewhat biased sample - public-facing figures working under the spotlight. Behind the scenes, many of us (myself included) quietly push the technology forward without seeking the camera. Personally, I remain skeptical that AGI is close at hand. It still feels very far away. Simple everyday tasks that humans perform effortlessly - such as cooking an egg - expose the enormous gap. A humanoid robot needs massive amounts of data and transfer learning just to handle basic variations: using a frying pan while standing on a mat, switching to a wok, dealing with smoke that obscures vision, or making real-time decisions under unpredictable constraints. AI lacks an intuitive prior understanding of the physical world, which is messy, contextual, and deeply complicated.This is precisely why projects like Stanford's Li Fei-Fei's World Lab are so important they aim to help AI develop a grounded comprehension of how the world actually works. Yet even these efforts remain preliminary, far from delivering a robust, full-fledged demonstration.This movie doesn't pretend to have all the answers, but it asks the right questions with honesty and nuance. Worth watching for anyone seriously interested in where humanity and artificial intelligence are headed..More like thisRelated interestsContribute to this pageSuggest an edit or add missing contentEdit pageMore to explore
